original_question: Does there exist a non-ample field K such that every finite split embedding problem over K has a regular solution? Equivalently, does there exist a non-ample field K for which the Debes-Deschamps conjecture holds?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open question in Section 7, “The conjecture of Dèbes and Deschamps,” asking for the converse direction to Theorem 1.3: whether Conjecture 1.1 can hold over a field K that is not ample.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right object (a field K), the right negated hypothesis (K is non-ample), the right quantified property (every finite split embedding problem over K), and the right named conjectural framework (the Dèbes–Deschamps conjecture / Conjecture 1.1 specialized to K).
missing_details: The paper’s quantified property should be unpacked: a finite split embedding problem over K means a finite Galois extension L/K together with a split epimorphism α:H→Gal(L/K) of finite groups.
The phrase “has a regular solution” should be defined in the paper’s sense: one considers the induced embedding problem over K(t), where t is an indeterminate transcendental over K.
It should be explicit that the solution is a proper/surjective solution of the induced problem, with solution field F containing L(t).
Regularity should be stated relative to L: F is regular over L (equivalently, F∩\bar{L}=L inside a fixed separable closure).

To be fully stand-alone, the reformulation “the Dèbes–Deschamps conjecture holds for K” should be phrased as “K satisfies Conjecture 1.1,” since Conjecture 1.1 in the paper is stated as a property of arbitrary fields.
No Hilbertian or characteristic hypothesis is part of the question as stated here; the field K is arbitrary apart from being non-ample.
refined_question: Does there exist a field K that is not ample such that for every finite Galois extension L/K and every split epimorphism α:H→Gal(L/K) of finite groups, the induced finite split embedding problem (L(t)/K(t),α) admits a proper solution F/K(t) whose solution field F is regular over L, where t is transcendental over K?
equivalent_formulation: Does there exist a non-ample field K that satisfies Conjecture 1.1 of Dèbes and Deschamps?
justification: This is the paper-faithful sharpening of your draft. Conjecture 1.1 is the Dèbes–Deschamps statement about regular solvability of every finite split embedding problem; Theorem 1.3 gives Pop’s positive result for ample fields; and Section 7 raises the converse-direction issue, namely whether ampleness is really necessary. So your draft is aimed at exactly that Section 7 question, not at a broader neighboring problem such as the regular inverse Galois problem alone. The main improvement needed is only to spell out the paper’s definitions of “finite split embedding problem” and “regular solution” so the question is fully self-contained and uses the same scope as Conjecture 1.1.
